mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.75% over 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of at least 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls by at least 2% YoY
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered periods at 5% significance, or the mechanism fails during periods of high inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which depresses earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary shock, which increases real interest rates and erodes equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes at 5% significance, or the mechanism fails when inflation expectations are anchored.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered periods at 5% significance, or the mechanism fails during periods of high mortgage rates.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) over two months signals a labor market normalization after a shock, which initially boosts consumer confidence but later raises wage inflation, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days before reversing.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE also increases over two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes at 5% significance, or the mechanism fails when wage inflation spikes immediately.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals reduced household buffer capacity, which increases reliance on credit and debt servicing, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12-month moving average for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes at 5% significance, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong credit expansion.
